comparisons.peer_topic: Adaptive Computing and Embedded Systems Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with the launch of Versal Series Gen 2 devices, including Versal AI Edge and Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclosed major processor portfolio expansions in 2024 focused on data center and AI workloads. Intel launched the Xeon 6 processors featuring a hybrid architecture of Efficient-cores (E-Cores) and Performance-cores (P-Cores) to address scale-out and compute-intensive AI tasks respectively. Similarly, AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with Versal Series Gen 2 devices, integrating preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems. While Intel focused on CPU core architecture differentiation for general data center/AI, AMD highlighted integrated SoC solutions for embedded AI acceleration.

sentences.text: In 2024, we launched the Intel Xeon 6 processors with Efficient-cores (or E-Cores) and Performance-cores (or P-cores).

Our E-core processors feature single-threaded cores for scale-out, parallel workloads, while our P-core processors feature hyperthreaded cores and built-in matrix engines that are designed for more compute-intensive workloads such as AI.

We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center revenue and AI platform launches
comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% from fiscal year 2023, with approximately 40% attributed to AI inference. The company launched AI inference platforms, NVIDIA DGX Cloud, AI Foundations, and Spectrum-X to support generative AI and accelerated networking.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclosed the launch of new platforms and processors in 2024 specifically designed to support AI workloads in the data center. Intel launched the Intel Xeon 6 processors, noting that its P-cores feature built-in matrix engines designed for compute-intensive workloads such as AI. NVIDIA launched AI inference platforms and announced Spectrum-X, an accelerated networking platform for AI, with Data Center revenue heavily driven by AI inference. Both companies explicitly tied their 2024 product launches to the demand for AI acceleration and inference capabilities.

sentences.text: Our E-core processors feature single-threaded cores for scale-out, parallel workloads, while our P-core processors feature hyperthreaded cores and built-in matrix engines that are designed for more compute-intensive workloads such as AI.

In Data Center, we launched AI inference platforms that combine our full-stack inference software with NVIDIA Ada, NVIDIA Hopper and NVIDIA Grace Hopper processors optimized for generative AI, LLMs and other AI workloads.
We announced NVIDIA Spectrum-X, an accelerated networking platform for AI.
